sphinx-riddle.title: The Riddle of the Sphinx
sphinx-riddle.speaker: sphinx
sphinx-riddle.riddle: What walks on four legs in the morning, two at noon and three in the evening?
sphinx-riddle.hint: Think of a whole life, from baby to old age.
sphinx-riddle.success: Correct! The Sphinx shrieks and throws herself from her rock.

socratic-questions.title: Questions, questions
socratic-questions.speaker: socrates
socratic-questions.intro: Tell me, friend. I only ask questions. You answer as best you can.

options: Doing what is right even when you are afraid
follow: Is a soldier who does not understand the danger brave, or just foolish?
But a soldier who runs forward in the wrong battle: is he doing right? Who decides what is right?
Is a bully who wins every fight brave? And what of the one who loses but does not give in?
Who decides what each person deserves? And if you are wrong about it, is that still justice?
If the rules are unfair, is it just to follow them? Who makes the rules?
Then if the strong decide to hurt you, would that be just? You frown. Why?

options: Knowing what you do not know
follow: A man may know every fact and still choose badly. Is he wise?
Ah. And how many people do you know who admit that?
The sophists thought so. Did they ever change their own minds?

socratic-questions.end: So you don't know either. Neither do I. Now we are both wiser.

perfect-circle.title: The perfect circle
perfect-circle.speaker: plato
perfect-circle.intro: Draw me a perfect circle. One stroke, in the sand.
perfect-circle.verdict: Close, but only the Idea is perfect.
perfect-circle.verdictHigh: Remarkable. Yet still only a shadow of the Idea.
perfect-circle.low: That is not yet a circle. Close it up and try again.

ball-drop.title: The falling balls
ball-drop.speaker: aristotle
ball-drop.intro: Two balls, one lead, one wood, dropped from a tall tower. Which lands first?

after.lead: That's what I thought too, for 1,800 years.
after.wood: Wood first? No. Look: they land together.
after.both: Correct, and it took the world a long while to check. Simon Stevin did, in 1586.
